role: Pure, Sendable overnight statistics computation for OvernightChartsView (RR→HR, rolling RMSSD, peak HRV, sleep duration, organized-zone fallback with archive backfill), with every sleep boundary moved onto the beats' t_ms axis (tMs(forSessionOffset:)), plus the view extension that fetches Apple Watch HR from HealthKit for sleep segments the Polar recording does not cover.
types: OvernightStatsComputer: struct — Sendable value holding session/result/healthKitSleep that computes OvernightStats off the main actor
OvernightStatsComputer.StatsInputs: struct (private) — bundle of inputs for makeStats (nadir/peak optional: nil when no HR survived)
OvernightStatsComputer.WindowFields: struct (private) — analysis window ms bounds and clock labels
OvernightStatsComputer.AnalysisWindow: struct (private) — analysis window ms and wall-clock dates
OvernightChartsView: extension — HealthKit HR gap-fill fetch helpers
SleepDurationFields: struct — minutes/formatted/deep/awakenings/efficiency/isFromHealthKit for the sleep card
toplevel: Only type declarations; OvernightStatsComputer conforms to Sendable so it can be captured by Task.detached in OvernightChartsView.loadOvernightStats.

flags.text: No unit test references OvernightStatsComputer, trimmedMeanHR, uncoveredWindows or any helper here; only OvernightSnapshotTests renders OvernightChartsView, whose stats load in an async .task.

units.does: Builds OvernightStats from session.rrSeries: resolves sleep bounds and segment ranges on the t_ms axis, computes full-recording and sleep-window HR (sleepHR), nadir/peak HR (nil when no HR), rolling RMSSD, then delegates assembly to makeStats. Returns OvernightStats.empty only when there are no RR points; with no HR the HRV side is still computed.

Full-recording HR values (computeHRValues over the whole series, stored HR when any beat has it, else 10 s RR windows) and sleep-window HR values (sleepWindowHRValues, falling back to the full set). Both empty when no beat yields a plausible HR.

Assembles OvernightStats: the peak-search band (peakSearchBand of the resolved sleep window), peak HRV/avg RMSSD from findPeakHRV in that band, nadir/min/max/trimmed-mean HR (0 with an empty nadir time when no HR), window fields, sleep-duration fields, chart start/end, organized recovery zones, and peakSearchBandMs (the band, only when the night has known sleep boundaries). The peak time label is empty when there is no rolling RMSSD; healthKitHR starts empty.
Resolves the analysis window via analysisWindowTimes and formats its start/end clock labels.
Forwards to deriveSleepDuration with the first point's t_ms and recording duration.

Returns HR values inside the sleep period: per-segment union (sorted by index) on split nights, else the single sleepStart..sleepEnd range; falls back to the caller's full-recording set when that yields nothing.

branches.cond: more than one sleep segment range
branches.effect: true: compute HR per segment and concatenate, sorted by index; false: single range sleepStartMs..sleepEndMs
true: log and use fallback (full recording HR); false: return filtered

units.does: Trimmed mean (5th–95th percentile) of the HR values once there are 10 or more, plain mean below that, 0 when there are none.
Computes analysis window ms bounds, preferring result.windowStartMs/EndMs, else indexing points by result.windowStart/windowEnd, and converts both to wall-clock dates.

branches.cond: result carries both windowStartMs and windowEndMs
branches.effect: true: use them; false: derive from indices
true: points[windowEnd].t_ms; false: last point t_ms, or 0 when no points (?? fallback)

units.does: Chart start ms: first RR point, or the earlier of that and the earliest segment start on split nights.

branches.cond: fewer than 2 segment ranges or no min
branches.effect: return firstPoint.t_ms; else min(firstPoint.t_ms, earliest segment start)

units.does: Chart end ms: last RR point end, or the later of that and the latest segment end on split nights.

branches.cond: fewer than 2 segment ranges or no max
branches.effect: return lastPoint.endMs; else max(lastPoint.endMs, latest segment end)

units.does: Returns result.organizedRecoveryZones, or computes them on demand when nil.

Returns organized recovery zones for a session from the in-memory cache entry for this sleep window, or runs WindowSelector.findBestWindow for its side effect and caches selector.lastOrganizedZones under the session and window. Internal (static) so other screens can share the fallback.

flags.text: Same cache-then-WindowSelector zone computation as RecoveryScoreDetailView.computeOrganizedZonesOnDemand (whose comment calls it 'Same fallback the legacy OvernightChartsView uses'). It is now internal; handoff b23 for RecoveryScoreDetailView to call it.

units.does: True when computeOvernightStats will run the on-demand zone scan: the result has no zones and the cache has none for this session's resolved sleep window. The view calls it before computing, to decide on the disk backfill.

branches.cond: result has zones or no beats

units.does: Fires a background detached task that persists computed zones into the archived session's analysisResult.

flags.text: docs/FLOWCHART.md says the on-demand organized-zone fallback re-runs the scan 'without rewriting the archive', but OvernightChartsView.loadOvernightStats calls backfillZonesToArchive, which re-archives the session with the computed zones (and posts flowRecoveryArchiveChanged).

units.does: Skips empty zones. Otherwise retrieves the archived session and, when its analysisResult has no zones, writes them through SessionArchive.update (read-check-write under the archive lock, re-checked by fillMissingZones; no same-night merge, no re-upload request). Errors are logged.

branches.cond: not archived or zones already present

units.does: True when the session has an analysis result whose organizedRecoveryZones is nil.
Sets the session's analysisResult.organizedRecoveryZones to zones when zonesMissing; otherwise leaves it.

branches.cond: zones already present or no result

units.does: Sleep start/end on the t_ms axis: HealthKit sleep when it has both bounds (offsets from session.startDate moved by onBeatClock, start ≥ 0, end ≤ last beat), else the stored session.sleepStartMs/EndMs (moved by onBeatClock; start 0 and end = last beat when missing or inverted).

branches.cond: HealthKit sleep has start and end
branches.effect: HK bounds, clamped to the recording

units.does: True when HealthKit sleep has both bounds, else when the session stores both sleepStartMs and sleepEndMs.

Per-segment sleep ranges on the t_ms axis (onBeatClock): HealthKit's effective segments when more than one, else the session's stored sleepSegments when more than one, else the single resolveSleepBoundaries envelope. Not clamped to the recording, so the chart can extend over HK sleep outside it.
tMs(forSessionOffset:series:sessionStart:) with this session's start date.

Moves a session-clock offset (ms after sessionStart, as HealthKit dates and stored sleep fields are) onto the beats' t_ms axis: finds the beat nearest that wall-clock time (RRSeries.indexClosestToWallClock) and shifts the offset by that beat's drift, t_ms − (wallClockMs + series-start shift). Streamed t_ms falls behind the wall clock after a Bluetooth drop; past either end of the recording the end beat's drift applies. Unchanged when the nearest beat has no wall-clock stamp (strap recordings, DataSourceSelector-rebased sessions).

branches.cond: no beats or nearest beat has no wallClockMs

units.does: Dispatches to stored per-beat HR or RR-window derived HR for an optional range.
Collects stored per-beat HR within [rangeStart, rangeEnd] for non-artifact beats with 30–200 bpm.

branches.cond: rangeStart set and point before it
rangeEnd set and point after it

branches.effect: isArtifact from flags; beyond flags → treated as clean

branches.cond: artifact, no hr, or hr outside 30–200

units.does: Derives HR from ~10 s RR windows stepping at most 5 beats at a time within the optional range; windows need ≥5 clean beats and 30–200 bpm.

branches.cond: rangeStart set and point before it
rangeEnd set and point past it

branches.effect: step 5 beats; else step to window.nextIndex

units.does: Converts a beat window to bpm; nil for <5 beats, zero duration, or outside 30–200 bpm.
Accumulates clean beats (non-artifact, RR 300–2000 ms) forward from idx until 10 s of RR time or the range end; returns count, summed duration, next index.

branches.cond: j in bounds, point within range, duration under 10 s

branches.effect: count beat and add RR; else skip beat

units.does: Rolling RMSSD: for every 30th beat (last step snapped to final point) computes RMSSD over a 300-beat window centred on it via TimeDomainAnalyzer.peakScanRMSSD.

branches.effect: loop; empty series gives -1 so no iterations

branches.cond: not at last point and next step overshoots
branches.effect: snap i to last index; else i += 30

flags.text: docs/FLOWCHART.md says rolling RMSSD uses 5-min windows; code uses a 300-beat window (duration varies with HR).

units.does: Peak rolling RMSSD among samples whose t_ms falls inside band (over all samples when none does) and the mean rolling RMSSD (0 when empty).

flags.text: The PDF report reimplements the rolling 300-beat/30-step peak RMSSD scan (OvernightReportRenderer.calculatePeakRMSSD/scanForPeakRMSSD) with the 30-70% band taken over the recording only, while the screen takes it over the HealthKit sleep span when present; the PDF's peak RMSSD and its time can differ from the Overnight screen's Peak HRV card for the same night. (Handoff b23: the PDF to take its band from OvernightStatsComputer.peakSearchBand.)

units.does: The 30–70% slice of [sleepStartMs, sleepEndMs] (the resolved sleep window on the t_ms axis: HealthKit, else stored sleep, else the recording) — the peak-HRV search band and the chart's 30%/70% markers.
Sleep duration fields from HealthKit (night minutes, deep minutes, awake periods, measured efficiency) when available, else the recording-length estimate.

branches.cond: HK sleep present and healthKitSleepMinutes non-nil
branches.effect: HealthKit fields with isFromHealthKit true; else estimatedSleepFromRecording

units.does: Counts HK awake stage intervals whose start is strictly inside sleepStart..sleepEnd; nil without stages or bounds.

branches.cond: no stage intervals or missing bounds
branches.effect: nil (no awakenings card); else the count

units.does: Night sleep minutes from HealthKit (excluding naps), else the boundary span in minutes, else nil.

branches.effect: nil; else (end-start)/60 which includes awake time inside the span

units.does: Builds SleepDurationFields from RecordingSleepEstimate for the recording minutes (90%/85% share), with deep/awakenings nil and isFromHealthKit false.
Formats minutes via LocalizedDuration.hoursMinutes.
Formats a date with the shared clock-time formatter.

For each HK sleep segment (as ms from session start) that is plausible, computes the sub-windows outside the Polar recording and fetches HealthKit HR samples for each; returns all samples sorted by time.

flags.text: HealthKit segment bounds (wall-clock offsets from session.startDate) are compared against recordingStartMs/EndMs, which the caller takes from the beats' t_ms; on a streamed night whose t_ms drifted after BLE drops the uncovered sub-windows are shifted by that drift. The stats computer now moves sleep bounds with tMs(forSessionOffset:series:sessionStart:); this gap-fill path does not yet.

units.does: True when a segment duration is positive and at most 16 h; logs and returns false otherwise.
Returns the parts of a segment outside the recording: the whole segment if disjoint, else up to two sub-ranges before/after.

branches.cond: segment entirely before or after the recording

units.does: Fetches HealthKit HR samples for a sub-window (ms from session start) of at least 60 s and maps them to (ms offset, hr). A fetch error is logged as a warning and yields an empty list (the chart falls back to the Polar data alone).
